books.section: The New Left, Feminism, and the Counterculture

source: original; stimulus is a licensed photograph viewed before writing (see figures)

stimulus.source_note: Photograph: crowd at the Woodstock Music Festival, August 15, 1969. Photograph by Derek Redmond and Paul Campbell, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
stimulus.text: The photograph, taken on August 15, 1969, shows part of the huge crowd at the Woodstock Music Festival on a dairy farm in Bethel, New York. More than 400,000 young people gathered for three days of rock music.

stem: The photograph best shows which feature of the counterculture?

options.text: Its leaders ran for president in 1968
options.misconception: The photograph shows a festival crowd, not a presidential campaign.

options.text: Its members dressed in business suits
options.misconception: The photograph shows young people in casual dress, many shirtless, not business suits.

options.text: Its music was played only on the radio at night
options.misconception: The photograph shows a live festival, not a radio broadcast.

options.text: Young people gathered in huge crowds for rock music

rationales.A: The photograph shows a festival crowd, not a presidential campaign.
rationales.B: The photograph shows young people in casual dress, many shirtless, not business suits.
rationales.C: The photograph shows a live festival, not a radio broadcast.
rationales.D: The photograph shows a vast crowd of young people at a rock festival, which is the counterculture gathered in one place.
rationales.general:
1. Look at the crowd: hundreds of young people, packed together outdoors.
2. They face a stage, clapping, at a festival built on rock music and on being together in the open air.
3. A gathering that big, of the young, for music, is the counterculture made visible.
Remember: A crowd photograph answers what a movement looked like when its people came together.
